title.zh: 卷一 本紀第一 高祖
title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一 高祖 Volume 1 Annals 1: Gaozu

sentences.zh: 李淵高祖神堯大聖大光孝皇帝諱淵，字叔德，姓李氏，隴西成紀人也。

translations.literal: Li Yuan, the Emperor Gaozu Shen Yao Great Sage Great Luminous Filial, was taboo-named Yuan, courtesy name Shude, surname Li, a native of Longxi Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan, posthumously honored as Emperor Gaozu Shen Yao the Great Sage and Great Luminous Filial, bore the taboo name Yuan and the courtesy name Shude. His surname was Li, and he came from Chengji in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 其七世祖暠，當晉末，據秦、涼以自王，是為涼武昭王。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Gao, at the end of the Jin, held Qin and Liang and made himself king—he was Liang Wuzhao Wang.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor Gao, at the end of the Jin dynasty, seized Qin and Liang and made himself king. He is known as Prince Wuzhao of Liang.

sentences.zh: 暠生歆，歆為沮渠蒙遜所滅。

translations.literal: Gao begot Xin; Xin was destroyed by Juqu Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Gao had a son, Xin, who was overthrown and destroyed by Juqu Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 歆生重耳，魏弘農太守。

translations.literal: Xin begot Chong'er, Governor of Hongnong under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had a son, Chong'er, who served as Governor of Hongnong under Wei.

sentences.zh: 重耳生熙，金門鎮將，戍于武川，因留家焉。

translations.literal: Chong'er begot Xi, Jinmen Fort Commander, garrisoned at Wuchuan, and thus settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er had a son, Xi, who served as commander of Jinmen Fort. He was garrisoned at Wuchuan and settled his family there.

sentences.zh: 熙生天賜，為幢主。

translations.literal: Xi begot Tianci, who was a standard-bearer chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had a son, Tianci, who served as a standard-bearer chief.

sentences.zh: 天賜生虎，西魏時，賜姓大野氏，官至太尉，與李弼等八人佐周代魏有功，皆為柱國，號「八柱國家」。

translations.literal: Tianci begot Hu; in Western Wei times he was granted the surname Daye, rose to Grand Commandant, and with Li Bi and seven others aided Zhou in replacing Wei with merit—all became pillar statemen, called the "Eight Pillar Statemen Families."
translations.idiomatic: Tianci had a son, Hu. Under Western Wei he was granted the surname Daye and rose to Grand Commandant. With Li Bi and seven others he helped Zhou supplant Wei and won great merit. All eight became pillar statemen and were known as the "Eight Pillar Statemen Families."

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受魏禪，虎已卒，乃追錄其功，封唐國公，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication from Wei, Hu had already died; his merits were then recorded posthumously, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tang, posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Zhou accepted the abdication from Wei, Hu had already died. The court then recorded his merits posthumously, enfeoffed him as Duke of Tang, and gave him the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 襄公生昞，襲封唐公，周安州總管、柱國大將軍，卒，謚曰仁。

translations.literal: Duke Xiang begot Bing; he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Tang, was Zhou's Inspector-general of Anzhou and Pillar State Great General; he died, posthumous title Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang had a son, Bing, who inherited the title of Duke of Tang and served as Inspector-general of Anzhou and Pillar State Great General under Zhou. When he died he was given the posthumous title Ren.

sentences.zh: 仁公生高祖於長安，體有三乳，性寬仁，襲封唐公。

translations.literal: Duke Ren begot Gaozu in Chang'an; his body had three nipples, his nature was generous and benevolent, and he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ren fathered Gaozu in Chang'an. Gaozu's body bore three nipples, his nature was generous and humane, and he inherited the title of Duke of Tang.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝獨孤皇后，高祖之從母也，以故文帝與高祖相親愛。

translations.literal: Empress Dugu of Emperor Wen of Sui was Gaozu's mother's sister, and for this reason Emperor Wen and Gaozu were close and fond of each other.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu, consort of Emperor Wen of Sui, was Gaozu's mother's sister. For that reason Emperor Wen and Gaozu were close and deeply fond of each other.

sentences.zh: 文帝相周，復高祖姓李氏，以為千牛備身，事隋譙、隴二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen served as chancellor of Zhou, he restored Gaozu's surname to Li, made him a Thousand-Ox Guard attendant, and he served the prefects of Qiao and Long in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was chancellor of Zhou, he restored Gaozu's surname to Li and appointed him a Thousand-Ox Guard attendant. Gaozu then served under the prefects of Qiao and Long during Sui.

sentences.zh: 大業中，歷岐州刺史、滎陽樓煩二郡太守，召為殿內少監、衞尉少卿。

translations.literal: During Daye, he successively served as Inspector of Qizhou and Administrator of the two commanderies of Xingyang and Loufan, and was summoned to be Palace Director and Vice Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he served in turn as Inspector of Qizhou and as Administrator of the Xingyang and Loufan commanderies. He was then summoned to the capital as Palace Director and Vice Minister of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝征遼東，遣高祖督運糧於懷遠鎮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang campaigned against Liaodong, he dispatched Gaozu to supervise grain transport at Huaiyuan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang campaigned against Liaodong, he sent Gaozu to supervise grain transport at Huaiyuan Fort.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感將反，其兄弟從征遼者皆逃歸，高祖先覺以聞，煬帝遽班師，以高祖為弘化留守以禦玄感，詔關右諸郡兵皆受高祖節度。

translations.literal: Yang Xuangan was about to rebel; his brothers who had joined the Liaodong campaign all fled home. Gaozu discovered it first and reported it. Emperor Yang hastily withdrew his army, appointed Gaozu as garrison commander of Honghua to defend against Xuangan, and decreed that troops of all commanderies west of the pass were to obey Gaozu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan was plotting rebellion, and his brothers who had joined the Liaodong campaign all fled home. Gaozu discovered the plot first and reported it. Emperor Yang hurriedly withdrew his army, appointed Gaozu garrison commander of Honghua to resist Xuangan, and decreed that all troops in the commanderies west of the pass were to come under Gaozu's command.

sentences.zh: 是時，隋政荒，天下大亂，煬帝多以猜忌殺戮大臣。

translations.literal: At this time Sui governance was decadent, the realm was in great turmoil, and Emperor Yang often killed and executed ministers out of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sui governance had fallen into decay, the realm was in great turmoil, and Emperor Yang often killed ministers on suspicion.

sentences.zh: 嘗以事召高祖，高祖遇疾，不時謁。

translations.literal: Once he summoned Gaozu on some matter; Gaozu fell ill and did not come to audience in time.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Yang summoned Gaozu on some matter, but Gaozu fell ill and failed to attend in time.

sentences.zh: 高祖有甥王氏在後宮，煬帝問之，王氏對以疾，煬帝曰：「可得死否？

translations.literal: Gaozu had a maternal nephew's daughter, the Lady Wang, in the inner palace; Emperor Yang questioned her, and Lady Wang answered that he was ill. Emperor Yang said, "Can he not just die?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had a maternal nephew's daughter, Lady Wang, serving in the inner palace. Emperor Yang questioned her, and Lady Wang replied that Gaozu was ill. Emperor Yang said, "Can he not just die?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖聞之益懼，因縱酒納賂以自晦。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard this he grew ever more fearful, and therefore indulged in wine and accepted bribes to obscure himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard this, his fear only deepened. He therefore drowned himself in wine and accepted bribes to hide his true intentions.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜山西河東慰撫大使，擊龍門賊母端兒，射七十發皆中，賊敗去，而斂其尸以築京觀，盡得其箭於其尸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Hedong in Shanxi; he attacked the Longmen bandit Mu Duan'er, with seventy arrows all hitting their mark; the bandits were defeated and fled, and he gathered their corpses to build a victory mound and recovered all his arrows from their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Hedong in Shanxi. He attacked the Longmen bandit Mu Duan'er, and of seventy arrows he loosed, every one found its mark. The bandits were defeated and fled. He gathered their corpses to build a victory mound and recovered every one of his arrows from the dead.

sentences.zh: 又擊絳州賊柴保昌，降其眾數萬人。

translations.literal: He again attacked the Jiangzhou bandit Chai Baochang and accepted the surrender of tens of thousands of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: He again attacked the Jiangzhou bandit Chai Baochang and accepted the surrender of tens of thousands of his followers.

sentences.zh: 突厥犯塞，高祖與馬邑太守王仁恭擊之，隋兵少，不敵。

translations.literal: The Turks invaded the border; Gaozu and Mayi Administrator Wang Rengong attacked them; Sui troops were few and could not match the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided the frontier, Gaozu and Mayi Administrator Wang Rengong attacked them, but the Sui force was too small to prevail.

sentences.zh: 高祖選精騎二千為游軍，居處飯食隨水草如突厥，而射獵馳騁示以閒暇，別選善射者伏為奇兵。

translations.literal: Gaozu selected two thousand elite cavalry as a mobile force, whose dwelling and food followed grass and water like the Turks, while hunting and racing to show leisure; separately he chose skilled archers to lie in ambush as a surprise force.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu selected two thousand elite horsemen as a mobile force. They camped and fed where grass and water lay, just as the Turks did, and hunted and raced about to appear at ease. Separately he chose skilled archers to lie in ambush as a surprise force.

sentences.zh: 虜見高祖，疑不敢戰，高祖乘而擊之，突厥敗走。

translations.literal: The enemy saw Gaozu, suspected a trap and dared not fight; Gaozu seized the moment and attacked; the Turks were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy saw Gaozu, they suspected a trap and dared not give battle. Gaozu seized the moment and struck; the Turks were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 十三年，拜太原留守，擊高陽歷山飛賊甄翟兒于西河，破之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was appointed garrison commander of Taiyuan; he attacked the Gaoyang Lishan Fei bandit Zhen Zhai'er at Xihe and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed garrison commander of Taiyuan. He attacked the Gaoyang bandit Zhen Zhai'er, styled Lishan Fei, at Xihe and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 是時，煬帝南遊江都，天下盜起。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Yang toured south to Jiangdu, and bandits rose throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Yang traveled south to Jiangdu, and bandits rose up throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 高祖子世民知隋必亡，陰結豪傑，招納亡命，與晉陽令劉文靜謀舉大事。

translations.literal: Gaozu's son Shimin knew that Sui would perish; he secretly allied with bold men, recruited fugitives, and with Jinyang Magistrate Liu Wenjing plotted to raise a great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's son Shimin knew that Sui was doomed. He secretly won over bold men, recruited fugitives, and with Jinyang Magistrate Liu Wenjing plotted to raise a great rebellion.

sentences.zh: 計已決，而高祖未之知，欲以情告，懼不見聽。

translations.literal: The plan was settled, but Gaozu did not know of it; Shimin wished to tell him the truth but feared he would not be heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was settled, but Gaozu knew nothing of it. Shimin wanted to tell him plainly yet feared he would not be listened to.

sentences.zh: 高祖留守太原，領晉陽宮監，而所善客裴寂為副監，世民陰與寂謀，寂因選晉陽宮人私侍高祖。

translations.literal: Gaozu was garrison commander of Taiyuan and superintendent of Jinyang Palace; his favored guest Pei Ji was deputy superintendent. Shimin secretly plotted with Ji; Ji thereupon selected palace women from Jinyang Palace to attend Gaozu privately.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was garrison commander of Taiyuan and superintendent of Jinyang Palace, while his favored guest Pei Ji served as deputy superintendent. Shimin secretly plotted with Ji, and Ji thereupon selected palace women from Jinyang Palace to attend Gaozu in private.

sentences.zh: 高祖過寂飲酒，酒酣從容，寂具以大事告之，高祖大驚。

translations.literal: Gaozu went to Ji's to drink; when the wine had warmed them and talk flowed freely, Ji fully told him of the great enterprise, and Gaozu was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu went to Ji's home to drink. When the wine had warmed them and conversation flowed freely, Ji told him the whole plan, and Gaozu was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 寂曰：「正為宮人奉公，事發當誅，為此爾。

translations.literal: Ji said, "It is precisely because palace women attended you, sir—if the matter were exposed you would be executed; it is for this reason."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "It is precisely because palace women attended you, sir. If the matter were exposed, you would be executed. That is why we must act."

sentences.zh: 」世民因亦入白其事，高祖初陽不許，欲執世民送官，已而許之，曰：「吾愛汝，豈忍告汝邪？

translations.literal: Shimin thereupon also entered to report the matter; at first Gaozu pretended not to consent and wished to seize Shimin and turn him over to the authorities; then he consented and said, "I love you—how could I bear to inform on you?"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin thereupon entered and reported the matter as well. At first Gaozu pretended to refuse and wanted to seize Shimin and turn him over to the authorities. Then he consented and said, "I love you—how could I bear to inform on you?"

sentences.zh: 」然未有以發。

translations.literal: Yet there was no occasion by which to act.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there was still no occasion to act.

sentences.zh: 而所在盜賊益多，突厥數犯邊，高祖兵出無功，煬帝遣使者執高祖詣江都，高祖大懼。

translations.literal: Meanwhile bandits everywhere grew ever more numerous, the Turks repeatedly violated the border, Gaozu's campaigns yielded no success, and Emperor Yang dispatched envoys to seize Gaozu and bring him to Jiangdu; Gaozu was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile bandits grew ever more numerous everywhere, the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier, and Gaozu's campaigns brought no success. Emperor Yang dispatched envoys to seize Gaozu and bring him to Jiangdu, and Gaozu was greatly terrified.

sentences.zh: 世民曰：「事急矣，可舉事！

translations.literal: Shimin said, "The matter is urgent—we can raise our enterprise!"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said, "The crisis is upon us—we must rise now!"

sentences.zh: 」已而煬帝復馳使者赦止高祖，其事遂已。

translations.literal: Then Emperor Yang again sent a fast courier with a pardon stopping Gaozu's arrest, and the matter thereupon ended.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Yang again sent a fast courier with a pardon halting Gaozu's arrest, and the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 是時，劉武周起馬邑，林士弘起豫章，劉元進起晉安，皆稱皇帝；

translations.literal: At this time Liu Wuzhou rose at Mayi, Lin Shihong rose at Yuzhang, and Liu Yuanjin rose at Jin'an—all proclaimed themselves emperors;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Wuzhou rose at Mayi, Lin Shihong at Yuzhang, and Liu Yuanjin at Jin'an, and all proclaimed themselves emperors;

sentences.zh: 朱粲起南陽，號楚帝；

translations.literal: Zhu Can rose at Nanyang and styled himself Emperor of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can rose at Nanyang and styled himself Emperor of Chu;

sentences.zh: 李子通起海陵，號楚王；

translations.literal: Li Zitong rose at Hailing and styled himself King of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zitong rose at Hailing and styled himself King of Chu;

sentences.zh: 邵江海據岐州，號新平王；

translations.literal: Shao Jianghai held Qizhou and styled himself King of Xinping;
translations.idiomatic: Shao Jianghai held Qizhou and styled himself King of Xinping;

sentences.zh: 薛舉起金城，號西秦霸王；

translations.literal: Xue Ju rose at Jincheng and styled himself Overlord of Western Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju rose at Jincheng and styled himself Overlord of Western Qin;

sentences.zh: 郭子和起榆林，號永樂王；

translations.literal: Guo Zihe rose at Yulin and styled himself King of Yongle;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zihe rose at Yulin and styled himself King of Yongle;

sentences.zh: 竇建德起河間，號長樂王，王須拔起恆、定，號漫天王；

translations.literal: Dou Jiande rose at Hejian and styled himself King of Changle; Wang Xuba rose at Heng and Ding and styled himself King of Mantian;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande rose at Hejian and styled himself King of Changle, while Wang Xuba rose in Heng and Ding and styled himself King of Mantian;

sentences.zh: 汪華起新安，杜伏威起淮南，皆號吳王；

translations.literal: Wang Hua rose at Xin'an and Du Fuwei rose at Huainan—both styled themselves King of Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua rose at Xin'an and Du Fuwei at Huainan, and both styled themselves King of Wu;

sentences.zh: 李密起鞏，號魏公；

translations.literal: Li Mi rose at Gong and styled himself Duke of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi rose at Gong and styled himself Duke of Wei;

sentences.zh: 王德仁起鄴，號太公；

translations.literal: Wang Deren rose at Ye and styled himself Grand Duke;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Deren rose at Ye and styled himself Grand Duke;

sentences.zh: 左才相起齊郡，號博山公；

translations.literal: Zuo Caixiang rose at Qi Commandery and styled himself Duke of Boshan;
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Caixiang rose in Qi Commandery and styled himself Duke of Boshan;

sentences.zh: 羅藝據幽州，左難當據涇，馮盎據高、羅，皆號總管；

translations.literal: Luo Yi held Youzhou, Zuo Nandang held Jing, and Feng Ang held Gao and Luo—all styled themselves Inspector-generals;
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi held Youzhou, Zuo Nandang held Jing, and Feng Ang held Gao and Luo, and all styled themselves Inspector-generals;

sentences.zh: 梁師都據朔方，號大丞相；

translations.literal: Liang Shidu held Shuofang and styled himself Grand Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shidu held Shuofang and styled himself Grand Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 孟海公據曹州，號錄事；

translations.literal: Meng Haigong held Caozhou and styled himself Recorder;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Haigong held Caozhou and styled himself Recorder;

sentences.zh: 周文舉據淮陽，號柳葉軍；

translations.literal: Zhou Wenju held Huaiyang and styled himself Commander of the Willow-Leaf Army;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wenju held Huaiyang and styled himself Commander of the Willow-Leaf Army;

sentences.zh: 高開道據北平，張長愻據五原，周洮據上洛，楊士林據山南，徐圓朗據兗州，楊仲達據豫州，張善相據伊、汝，王要漢據汴州，時德叡據尉氏，李義滿據平陵，綦公順據青、萊，淳于難據文登，徐師順據任城，蔣弘度據東海，王薄據齊郡，蔣善合據鄆州，田留安據章丘，張青特據濟北，臧君相據海州，殷恭邃據舒州，周法明據永安，苗海潮據永嘉，梅知巖據宣城，鄧文進據廣州，俚酋楊世略據循、潮，冉安昌據巴東，甯長真據鬱林，其別號諸盜往往屯聚山澤。

translations.literal: Gao Kaidao held Beiping, Zhang Changsun held Wuyuan, Zhou Tao held Shangluo, Yang Shilin held Shannan, Xu Yuanlang held Yanzhou, Yang Zhongda held Yuzhou, Zhang Shanxiang held Yi and Ru, Wang Yaohan held Bianzhou, Shi Derui held Weishi, Li Yiman held Pingling, Qi Gongshun held Qing and Lai, Chunyu Nan held Wendeng, Xu Shishun held Rencheng, Jiang Hongdu held Donghai, Wang Bo held Qi Commandery, Jiang Shanhe held Yanzhou, Tian Liu'an held Zhangqiu, Zhang Qingte held Jibei, Zang Junxiang held Haizhou, Yin Gongdu held Shuzhou, Zhou Faming held Yong'an, Miao Haichao held Yongjia, Mei Zhiyan held Xuancheng, Deng Wenjin held Guangzhou, the Li chieftain Yang Shilue held Xun and Chao, Ran Anchang held Badong, Ning Changzhen held Yulin—the various other titled bandits often gathered and encamped in mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kaidao held Beiping; Zhang Changsun held Wuyuan; Zhou Tao held Shangluo; Yang Shilin held Shannan; Xu Yuanlang held Yanzhou; Yang Zhongda held Yuzhou; Zhang Shanxiang held Yi and Ru; Wang Yaohan held Bianzhou; Shi Derui held Weishi; Li Yiman held Pingling; Qi Gongshun held Qing and Lai; Chunyu Nan held Wendeng; Xu Shishun held Rencheng; Jiang Hongdu held Donghai; Wang Bo held Qi Commandery; Jiang Shanhe held Yanzhou; Tian Liu'an held Zhangqiu; Zhang Qingte held Jibei; Zang Junxiang held Haizhou; Yin Gongdu held Shuzhou; Zhou Faming held Yong'an; Miao Haichao held Yongjia; Mei Zhiyan held Xuancheng; Deng Wenjin held Guangzhou; the Li chieftain Yang Shilue held Xun and Chao; Ran Anchang held Badong; and Ning Changzhen held Yulin. The many other bandits with their own titles often gathered and encamped in mountains and marshes.

sentences.zh: 而劉武周攻汾陽宮，高祖乃集將吏告曰：「今吾為留守，而賊據離宮，縱賊不誅，罪當死。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Liu Wuzhou attacked Fenyang Palace; Gaozu thereupon assembled his generals and officials and told them, "I am now garrison commander, yet bandits hold the detached palace; if I release the bandits without punishing them, the crime merits death."
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Wuzhou attacked Fenyang Palace. Gaozu thereupon assembled his generals and officials and told them, "I am garrison commander here, yet bandits hold the detached palace. If I let the bandits go unpunished, the crime merits death."

sentences.zh: 然出兵必待報，今江都隔遠，後期奈何？

translations.literal: Yet to send troops one must await orders; now Jiangdu is far away—what if we are late?
translations.idiomatic: Yet to send troops we must await orders, and Jiangdu is far away. What are we to do if we arrive too late?

sentences.zh: 」將吏皆曰：「國家之利可專者，公也。

translations.literal: The generals and officials all said, "Where the state's interest may be decided on one's own authority, that authority is yours, sir."
translations.idiomatic: The generals and officials all said, "Where the state's interest may be decided on one's own authority, that authority rests with you, sir."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 」乃募兵，旬日間得眾一萬。

translations.literal: He thereupon recruited troops, and within ten days obtained ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon recruited troops, and within ten days gathered ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 副留守虎賁郎將王威、虎牙郎將高君雅見兵大集，疑有變，謀因禱雨晉祠以圖高祖。

translations.literal: The deputy garrison commanders, Tiger-Gallant Commandant Wang Wei and Tiger-Fang Commandant Gao Junya, seeing the great gathering of troops, suspected a plot and planned to use a rain-prayer at Jin Shrine to seize Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy garrison commanders, Tiger-Gallant Commandant Wang Wei and Tiger-Fang Commandant Gao Junya, seeing the great gathering of troops, suspected treachery and plotted to seize Gaozu under cover of a rain-prayer at Jin Shrine.

sentences.zh: 高祖覺之，乃陰為備。

translations.literal: Gaozu detected it and secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu detected the plot and secretly made preparations.

sentences.zh: 五月甲子，高祖及威、君雅視事，開陽府司馬劉政會告威、君雅反，即坐上執之。

translations.literal: On jiazi of the fifth month, Gaozu and Wei and Junya attended to business; Kaiyang Prefecture Major Liu Zhenghui accused Wei and Junya of rebellion, and they were seized on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi of the fifth month, Gaozu, Wei, and Junya attended to business together. Kaiyang Prefecture Major Liu Zhenghui accused Wei and Junya of rebellion, and they were seized on the spot.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，突厥犯邊，高祖令軍中曰：「人告威、君雅召突厥，今其果然。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Turks violated the border; Gaozu told the army, "Men reported that Wei and Junya summoned the Turks—now it has indeed come to pass."
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Turks raided the frontier. Gaozu told the army, "Men reported that Wei and Junya summoned the Turks, and now it has indeed come to pass."

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之以起兵。

translations.literal: He thereupon killed them and raised his army.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon executed them and raised his army in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 遣劉文靜使突厥，約連和。

translations.literal: He dispatched Liu Wenjing as envoy to the Turks to arrange an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Wenjing as envoy to the Turks to arrange a joint alliance.

sentences.zh: 六月己卯，傳檄諸郡，稱義兵，開大將軍府，置三軍。

translations.literal: On jimao of the sixth month, he issued proclamations to the commanderies, styled his force the Righteous Army, opened the Great General's Headquarters, and established three armies.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao of the sixth month he issued proclamations to the commanderies, styled his force the Righteous Army, opened the Great General's Headquarters, and established three armies.

sentences.zh: 以子建成為隴西公、左領軍大都督，左軍隸焉；

translations.literal: He made his son Jiancheng Duke of Longxi and Left Army Commander-in-chief, and the left army was placed under him;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his son Jiancheng Duke of Longxi and Left Army Commander-in-chief, with the left army placed under his command;

sentences.zh: 世民為燉煌公、右領軍大都督，右軍隸焉；

translations.literal: Shimin was made Duke of Dunhuang and Right Army Commander-in-chief, and the right army was placed under him;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin was made Duke of Dunhuang and Right Army Commander-in-chief, with the right army placed under his command;

sentences.zh: 元吉為姑臧公，中軍隸焉。

translations.literal: Yuanji was made Duke of Guzang, and the center army was placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was made Duke of Guzang, with the center army placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 裴寂為長史，劉文靜為司馬，石艾縣長殷開山為掾，劉政會為屬，長孫順德、王長諧、劉弘基、竇琮為統軍。

translations.literal: Pei Ji was made Chief Clerk, Liu Wenjing Marshal, Shi'ai County Magistrate Yin Kaishan Assistant, Liu Zhenghui Aide, and Zhangsun Shunde, Wang Changxie, Liu Hongji, and Dou Cong Army Controllers.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji served as Chief Clerk, Liu Wenjing as Marshal, Shi'ai County Magistrate Yin Kaishan as Assistant, Liu Zhenghui as Aide, and Zhangsun Shunde, Wang Changxie, Liu Hongji, and Dou Cong as Army Controllers.

sentences.zh: 開倉庫賑窮乏。

translations.literal: He opened the storehouses to relieve the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the storehouses to relieve the destitute.

sentences.zh: 七月壬子，高祖杖白旗，誓眾於野，有兵三萬，以元吉為太原留守。

translations.literal: On renzi of the seventh month, Gaozu bore a white flag and swore the host in the open field; he had thirty thousand troops and made Yuanji garrison commander of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi of the seventh month Gaozu bore a white flag and swore his troops in the open field. He had thirty thousand men and appointed Yuanji garrison commander of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，發太原。

translations.literal: On guichou, he set out from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he marched out from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，遣將張綸徇下離石、龍泉、文城三郡。

translations.literal: On jiayin, he dispatched the general Zhang Lun to subdue and take the three commanderies of Lishi, Longquan, and Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he dispatched General Zhang Lun to subdue the three commanderies of Lishi, Longquan, and Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，次靈石，營於賈胡堡。

translations.literal: On bingchen, he halted at Lingshi and encamped at Jiahu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he halted at Lingshi and encamped at Jiahu Fort.

sentences.zh: 隋虎牙郎將宋老生䤈邑，以拒義師。

translations.literal: Sui Tiger-Fang Commandant Song Laosheng encamped at Huoyi to resist the Righteous Army.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Tiger-Fang Commandant Song Laosheng encamped at Huoyi to resist the Righteous Army.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，隋鷹揚府司馬李軌起武威，號大涼王。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Sui Yingyang Prefecture Major Li Gui rose at Wuwei and styled himself King of Great Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Sui Yingyang Prefecture Major Li Gui rose at Wuwei and styled himself King of Great Liang.

sentences.zh: 八月辛巳，敗宋老生于霍邑。

translations.literal: On xinsi of the eighth month, he defeated Song Laosheng at Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi of the eighth month he defeated Song Laosheng at Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，下臨汾郡。

translations.literal: On bingxu, he took Linfen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu he captured Linfen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，克絳郡。

translations.literal: On xinmao, he captured Jiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he captured Jiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，次龍門，突厥來來逆。

translations.literal: On guisi, he halted at Longmen; the Turks came to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he halted at Longmen, and the Turks came to intercept.

sentences.zh: 九月戊午，高祖領太尉，加置僚佐。

translations.literal: On wuwu of the ninth month, Gaozu assumed the post of Grand Commandant and added staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu of the ninth month Gaozu assumed the post of Grand Commandant and added staff officers.

sentences.zh: 以少牢祀河，乃濟。

translations.literal: He offered lesser sacrifices to the river and then crossed.
translations.idiomatic: He offered lesser sacrifices to the river and then crossed.

sentences.zh: 甲子，次長春宮。

translations.literal: On jiazi, he halted at Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he halted at Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，隴西公建成、劉文靜屯永豐倉，守潼關。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Duke of Longxi Jiancheng and Liu Wenjing encamped at Yongfeng Granary and guarded Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Duke of Longxi Jiancheng and Liu Wenjing encamped at Yongfeng Granary to guard Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 燉煌公世民自渭北徇三輔，從父弟神通起兵于鄠，柴氏婦，高祖女也，亦起兵于司竹，皆與世民會。

translations.literal: Duke of Dunhuang Shimin from north of the Wei subdued the Three Adjuncts; his father's younger brother Tong rose in arms at Hu, and the Lady Chai, Gaozu's daughter, also rose in arms at Sizhu—all joined Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Dunhuang Shimin marched from north of the Wei to subdue the Three Adjuncts. His father's younger brother Tong rose in arms at Hu, and Lady Chai, Gaozu's daughter, also rose at Sizhu. All joined Shimin.

sentences.zh: 郿賊丘師利李仲文、盩厔賊何潘仁向善思、宜君賊劉炅等皆來降，因略定鄠、杜。

translations.literal: The Mei bandits Qiu Shili and Li Zhongwen, the Zhouzhi bandits He Panren and Xiang Sian, the Yijun bandit Liu Jiong, and others all came to surrender, and he thereby pacified Hu and Du.
translations.idiomatic: The Mei bandits Qiu Shili and Li Zhongwen, the Zhouzhi bandits He Panren and Xiang Sian, the Yijun bandit Liu Jiong, and others all came to surrender, and he thereby pacified Hu and Du.

sentences.zh: 壬申，高祖次馮翊。

translations.literal: On renshen, Gaozu halted at Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Gaozu halted at Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，燉煌公世民屯阿城，隴西公建成自新豐趨霸上。

translations.literal: On yihai, Duke of Dunhuang Shimin encamped at Acheng, and Duke of Longxi Jiancheng from Xinfeng hastened toward Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Duke of Dunhuang Shimin encamped at Acheng, while Duke of Longxi Jiancheng marched from Xinfeng toward Bashang.

sentences.zh: 丙子，高祖自下邽以西，所經隋行宮、苑籞，悉罷之，出宮女還其家。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Gaozu from Xiaji westward, at every Sui traveling palace and park enclosure he passed, abolished them all and released palace women to return home.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, from Xiaji westward, Gaozu abolished every Sui traveling palace and park enclosure he passed through and released the palace women to return home.

sentences.zh: 十月辛巳，次長樂宮，有眾二十萬。

translations.literal: On xinsi of the tenth month, he halted at Changle Palace; he had two hundred thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi of the tenth month he halted at Changle Palace with two hundred thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 隋留守衞文昇等奉代王侑守京城，高祖遣使諭之，不報。

translations.literal: Sui garrison commanders Wei Wensheng and others, supporting Prince Dai You, defended the capital; Gaozu dispatched envoys to instruct them, but they did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Sui garrison commanders Wei Wensheng and others, supporting Prince Dai You, defended the capital. Gaozu sent envoys to instruct them, but they did not reply.

sentences.zh: 乃圍城，下令曰：「犯隋七廟及宗室者，罪三族。

translations.literal: He thereupon besieged the city and issued an order saying, "Whoever violates the seven temples of Sui and the imperial clan shall be punished to the third degree of kin."
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon besieged the city and issued an order: "Whoever violates the seven temples of Sui and the imperial clan shall be punished to the third degree of kin."

sentences.zh: 」丙申，隋羅山令蕭銑自號梁公。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Sui Luoshan Magistrate Xiao Xian styled himself Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Sui Luoshan Magistrate Xiao Xian styled himself Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙辰，克京城。

translations.literal: On bingchen of the eleventh month, he captured the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen of the eleventh month he captured the capital.

sentences.zh: 命主符郎宋公弼收圖籍。

translations.literal: He ordered Master of Tallies Song Gongbi to collect maps and registers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Master of Tallies Song Gongbi to collect the maps and registers.

sentences.zh: 約法十二條，殺人、劫盜、背軍、叛者死。

translations.literal: He established twelve articles of law: murder, robbery, desertion, and rebellion were punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: He promulgated twelve articles of law. Murder, robbery, desertion, and rebellion were punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，遙尊隋帝為太上皇，立代王為皇帝。

translations.literal: On guihai, he honored the Sui emperor from afar as Retired Emperor and installed Prince Dai as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he honored the Sui emperor from afar as Retired Emperor and installed Prince Dai as emperor.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元義寧。

translations.literal: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yining.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yining.

sentences.zh: 甲子，高祖入京師，至朝堂，望闕而拜。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Gaozu entered the capital, reached the court hall, and bowed toward the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Gaozu entered the capital, came to the court hall, and bowed toward the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 隋帝授高祖假黃鉞、使持節、大都督內外諸軍事、大丞相、錄尚書事，進封唐王。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor invested Gaozu with the provisional yellow axe, credentials as envoy holding staff, supreme command over all military affairs within and without, the post of Grand Chancellor, and charge over the Secretariat, and advanced his enfeoffment to Prince of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor invested Gaozu with the provisional yellow axe, credentials as envoy holding staff, supreme command over all military affairs within and without, the post of Grand Chancellor, and charge over the Secretariat, and advanced his enfeoffment to Prince of Tang.

sentences.zh: 以武德殿為丞相府，下教曰令，視事于虔化門。

translations.literal: He made Wude Hall the chancellor's headquarters, styled his edicts as orders, and conducted business at Qianhua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He made Wude Hall the chancellor's headquarters, styled his edicts as orders, and conducted business at Qianhua Gate.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸未，隋帝贈唐襄公為景王；

translations.literal: On guiwei of the twelfth month, the Sui emperor posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Xiang of Tang as Prince Jing;
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei of the twelfth month, the Sui emperor posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Xiang of Tang as Prince Jing;

sentences.zh: 仁公為元王；

translations.literal: Duke of Ren as Prince Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Ren as Prince Yuan;

sentences.zh: 夫人竇氏為唐國妃，謚曰穆。

translations.literal: Lady Dou was made consort of the State of Tang, with posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Dou was made consort of the State of Tang, with the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 以建成為唐國世子；

translations.literal: Jiancheng was made heir of the State of Tang;
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng was made heir of the State of Tang;

sentences.zh: 世民為唐國內史，徙封秦國公；

translations.literal: Shimin was made Director of the Secretariat for the State of Tang and was transferred to be enfeoffed as Duke of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin was made Director of the Secretariat for the State of Tang and was transferred to Duke of Qin;

sentences.zh: 元吉為齊國公。

translations.literal: Yuanji was made Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was made Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 丞相府置長史、司錄以下官。

translations.literal: The Chancellor's office was staffed with a Chief Administrator, Director of Records, and officials below them.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's office was staffed with a chief administrator, director of records, and subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 趙郡公孝恭徇山南。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong campaigned to pacify south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong campaigned to pacify the lands south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，雲陽令詹俊徇巴、蜀。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Yunyang Magistrate Zhan Jun campaigned to pacify Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Yunyang Magistrate Zhan Jun campaigned to pacify Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 二年正月丁未，隋帝詔唐王劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，加前後羽葆、鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, on dingwei, the Sui emperor decreed that the Prince of Tang might wear sword and shoes in the hall, need not hasten when entering court, and need not have his name spoken when being saluted; front and rear feathered canopies and musical escort were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, on dingwei the Sui emperor decreed that the Prince of Tang might enter the hall wearing sword and shoes, need not hurry when attending court, and need not have his name spoken when being saluted; feathered canopies and musical escort were added before and behind him.

sentences.zh: 戊午，周洮降。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Zhou Tao surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Zhou Tao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，世子建成為左元帥，秦國公世民為右元帥，徇地東都。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Heir Jiancheng was made Left Grand Marshal, Duke of Qin Shimin Right Grand Marshal, to pacify the lands around the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Heir Jiancheng was made Left Grand Marshal and Duke of Qin Shimin Right Grand Marshal, to pacify the lands around the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 二月己卯，太常卿鄭元璹定樊、鄧，使者馬元規徇荊、襄。

translations.literal: In the second month on jimao, Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshu pacified Fan and Deng; envoy Ma Yuangui campaigned in Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month on jimao Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshu pacified Fan and Deng, while envoy Ma Yuangui campaigned in Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 三月己酉，齊國公元吉為太原道行軍元帥。

translations.literal: In the third month on jiyou, Duke of Qi Yuanji was made Grand Marshal of the Taiyuan Circuit campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month on jiyou Duke of Qi Yuanji was made Grand Marshal of the Taiyuan Circuit campaign.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，世民徙封趙國公。

translations.literal: On yimao, Shimin was transferred to be enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Shimin was transferred to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，隋右屯衞將軍宇文化及弒太上皇于江都，立秦王浩為皇帝。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Sui Right Garrison Commander Yuwen Huaji assassinated the Retired Emperor at Jiangdu and installed Prince of Qin Hao as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Sui Right Garrison Commander Yuwen Huaji assassinated the Retired Emperor at Jiangdu and installed Prince of Qin Hao as emperor.

sentences.zh: 吳興郡守沈法興據丹陽，自稱江南道總管。

translations.literal: Wuxing Commandery Administrator Shen Faxing seized Danyang and styled himself Overall Administrator of the Jiangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing Commandery Administrator Shen Faxing seized Danyang and styled himself Overall Administrator of the Jiangnan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 樂安人盧祖尚據光州，自稱刺史。

translations.literal: Lu Zushang of Lean occupied Guang Prefecture and styled himself Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zushang of Lean occupied Guang Prefecture and styled himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，隋帝進唐王位相國，總百揆，備九錫，唐國置丞相等官，立四廟。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the Sui emperor advanced the Prince of Tang to Chancellor, supreme over all government affairs, endowed with the Nine Bestowals; the State of Tang was given a Chancellor and other offices, and four ancestral temples were established.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the Sui emperor advanced the Prince of Tang to Chancellor with supreme authority over all government affairs and endowed him with the Nine Bestowals; the State of Tang was given a chancellor and other offices, and four ancestral temples were established.

sentences.zh: 四月己卯，張長愻降。

translations.literal: In the fourth month on jimao, Zhang Changxun surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month on jimao Zhang Changxun surrendered.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，停竹使符，班銀菟符。

translations.literal: On xinsi, bamboo envoy tallies were discontinued and silver rabbit tallies were distributed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi bamboo envoy tallies were discontinued and silver rabbit tallies were issued.

sentences.zh: 五月乙巳，隋帝命唐王冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on yisi, the Sui emperor ordered the Prince of Tang to wear a twelve-tassel crown, erect the imperial banners, and receive the imperial procession guard when going out and returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month on yisi the Sui emperor ordered the Prince of Tang to wear a twelve-tassel crown, raise the imperial banners, and receive the imperial procession guard when going out and returning.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，王德仁降。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Wang Deren surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Wang Deren surrendered.

sentences.zh: 戊午，隋帝遜于位，以刑部尚書蕭造、司農少卿裴之隱奉皇帝璽紱於唐王，三讓乃受。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Sui emperor abdicated; Minister of Justice Xiao Zao and Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Zhiyin presented the imperial seal and cord to the Prince of Tang, who declined three times before accepting.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the Sui emperor abdicated; Minister of Justice Xiao Zao and Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Zhiyin presented the imperial seal and cord to the Prince of Tang, who declined three times before accepting.

sentences.zh: 武德元年五月甲子，即皇帝位于太極殿。

translations.literal: On jiazi of the fifth month of the first year of Wude, he ascended the throne in the Hall of Supreme Pivot.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi of the fifth month of the first year of Wude, Gaozu ascended the throne in the Hall of Supreme Pivot.

sentences.zh: 命蕭造兼太尉，告于南郊，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: He appointed Xiao Zao concurrently as Grand Commandant, announced this at the Southern Suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Xiao Zao concurrently as Grand Commandant, announced the accession at the Southern Suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 賜百官、庶人爵一級，義師所過給復三年，其餘給復一年。

translations.literal: He granted one rank of nobility to all officials and commoners; areas passed through by the righteous army received three years of tax and corvée exemption, the rest one year.
translations.idiomatic: He granted one rank of nobility to all officials and commoners; regions traversed by the righteous army received three years of tax and corvée exemption, and all others one year.

sentences.zh: 改郡為州，太守為刺史。

translations.literal: Commanderies were changed to prefectures, and commandery governors to prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies were renamed prefectures, and commandery governors became prefects.

sentences.zh: 庚午，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Venus was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Venus was visible in the daytime.

sentences.zh: 隋東都留守元文都及左武衞大將軍王世充立越王侗為皇帝。

translations.literal: Sui Eastern Capital garrison commander Yuan Wendu and Left Martial Guard General Wang Shichong installed Prince of Yue Tong as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Eastern Capital garrison commander Yuan Wendu and Left Martial Guard General Wang Shichong installed Prince of Yue Yang Tong as emperor.

sentences.zh: 六月甲戌，趙國公世民為尚書令，裴寂為尚書右僕射、知政事，劉文靜為納言，隋民部尚書蕭瑀、丞相府司錄參軍竇威為內史令。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Duke of Zhao Shimin was made Director of the Secretariat; Pei Ji was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of Affairs; Liu Wenjing was made Director of the Department of State Affairs; former Sui Minister of the Household Xiao Yu and Chancellor's Office Director of Records Dou Wei were made Directors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Duke of Zhao Shimin was made Director of the Secretariat; Pei Ji was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with charge of affairs; Liu Wenjing was made Director of the Department of State Affairs; former Sui Minister of the Household Xiao Yu and Chancellor's Office Director of Records Dou Wei were made Directors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丙子，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Venus was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Venus was visible in the daytime.

sentences.zh: 己卯，追謚皇高祖曰宣簡公；

translations.literal: On jimao, the imperial great-great-grandfather was posthumously titled Duke Xuanjian;
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the imperial great-great-grandfather was posthumously titled Duke Xuanjian;

sentences.zh: 皇曾祖曰懿王；

translations.literal: the imperial great-grandfather as Prince Yi;
translations.idiomatic: the imperial great-grandfather as Prince Yi;

sentences.zh: 皇祖曰景皇帝，廟號太祖，祖妣梁氏曰景烈皇后；

丁巳，太白晝見。
壬戌，吐谷渾請和。

謚曰太武，廟號高祖。
上元元年，改謚神堯皇帝。
天寶八戴，謚神堯大聖皇帝；
十三載，增謚神堯大聖大光孝皇帝。
贊曰：自古受命之君，非有德不王。
自夏后氏以來，始傳以世，而有賢有不肖，故其為世，數亦或短或長。
論者乃謂周自后稷至於文、武，積功累仁，其來也遠，故其為世尤長。
然考於世本，夏、商、周皆出於黃帝，夏自鯀以前，商自契至於成湯，其間寂寥無聞，與周之興異矣。
而漢亦起於亭長叛亡之徒。
及其興也，有天下皆數百年而後已。
由是言之，天命豈易知哉！
然考其終始治亂，顧其功德有厚薄與其制度紀綱所以維持者如何，而其後世，或寖以隆昌，或遽以壞亂，或漸以陵遲，或能振而復起，或遂至於不可支持，雖各因其勢，然有德則興，無德則絕，豈非所謂天命者常不顯其符，而俾有國者兢兢以自勉耶？
唐在周、隋之際，世雖貴矣，然烏有所謂積功累仁之漸，而高祖之興，亦何異因時而特起者歟？
雖其有治有亂，或絕或微，然其有天下年幾三百，可謂盛哉！
豈非人厭隋亂而蒙德澤，繼以太宗之治，制度紀綱之法，後世有以憑藉扶持，而能永其天命歟？
